concepts.title: Rectilinear Propagation of Light
concepts.definition: Light naturally travels in a straight path and does not curve around objects in its way.
concepts.key_idea: Light follows a linear trajectory from the source.
question_patterns: how does light travel
why can we not see a candle through a bent pipe
demonstrate that light travels in straight lines
describe the path of light
state two key points about rectilinear propagation of light

solution_steps.explain: Look at a light source through a straight tube.
Attempt to look at the same source through a bent tube; the light is blocked.
Since light is only visible through a straight path, light travels in straight lines.

concepts.title: Reflection of Light
concepts.definition: The phenomenon where a surface, like a mirror or water, changes the direction of light hitting it.
concepts.key_idea: Shiny surfaces act as mirrors to redirect light.
question_patterns: define reflection of light
State clearly what happens means in this chapter and why it matters.
how can we change the direction of light
give examples of reflecting surfaces
what do you understand by reflection of light

solution_steps.explain: Locate a polished or shiny surface like a mirror.
Observe the light hitting the surface and bouncing off in a new direction.
Confirm that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, proving the law of reflection.

concepts.title: Image Formation in a Plane Mirror
concepts.definition: A flat mirror creates an upright image that is indeed the same size as the object and located at an equal distance behind the mirror.
concepts.key_idea: The image in a plane mirror is virtual, erect, and equidistant.
question_patterns: calculate the distance of the image from the mirror
what are the characteristics of a plane mirror image
find the distance between the object and its image
is the image in a plane mirror real or virtual
find the required value in a image formation in a plane mirror problem

solution_steps.explain: Measure the distance from the object to the mirror surface.
The total distance between object and image is the sum of their distances from the mirror.
Confirm the image is virtual, erect, same size, and laterally inverted as expected for a plane mirror.

concepts.title: Real and Virtual Images
concepts.definition: A real image can indeed be captured on a screen, while a virtual image cannot be projected onto a surface.
concepts.key_idea: Real images are formed by converging rays; virtual images are perceived behind mirrors.
question_patterns: difference between real and virtual image
can a plane mirror form a real image
define a virtual image
how to identify a real image
how does real and virtual images work

solution_steps.explain: Place a screen at the point where the image appears to form.
If the image appears on the screen, it is real; if not, it is virtual.
Use the screen test result to conclude whether the image is real (captured on screen) or virtual (not captured).

concepts.title: Concave Mirrors
concepts.definition: A spherical mirror with an inward-curving reflecting surface that can form real or virtual images depending on object distance.
concepts.key_idea: Concave mirrors converge light and are used by both dentists and in torch reflectors.
question_patterns: uses of concave mirrors
what type of image does a concave mirror form
which mirror is used by dentists
can a concave mirror form a virtual image
list the main features of concave mirrors

solution_steps.explain: Identify if the reflecting surface curves inward like a spoon's bowl.
Observe that close objects appear magnified and erect, while distant objects appear inverted.
Recognize uses such as dentist mirrors, torch reflectors, and shaving mirrors that rely on the converging property of concave mirrors.

concepts.title: Convex Mirrors
concepts.definition: A spherical mirror with an outward-curving reflecting surface that always produces virtual, erect, and diminished images.
concepts.key_idea: Convex mirrors provide a wide field of view, making them ideal for vehicle side mirrors.
question_patterns: why are convex mirrors used as side mirrors
describe the image formed by a convex mirror
can a convex mirror form a real image
identify a mirror that always forms smaller images
give one everyday example of convex mirrors

solution_steps.explain: Identify if the reflecting surface curves outward.
Observe that the image is always upright and smaller than the object.
Verify that the convex mirror shows a wider area than a plane mirror, making it suitable for side mirrors of vehicles.

concepts.title: Convex Lenses
concepts.definition: A transparent lens fatter in the middle than at the edges that converges light rays.
concepts.key_idea: Convex lenses can magnify objects and are used in magnifying glasses.
question_patterns: what is a magnifying glass
describe a convex lens
does a convex lens converge or diverge light
what kind of image is formed by a convex lens
give one everyday example of convex lenses

solution_steps.explain: Check if the lens is thicker in the center than at the periphery.
Note that parallel light rays passing through the lens meet at a point.
Hold the lens close to an object and observe the enlarged, erect virtual image, confirming it acts as a magnifying glass.

concepts.title: Concave Lenses
concepts.definition: A transparent lens slimmer in the middle than at the edges that diverges light rays.
concepts.key_idea: Concave lenses always form virtual, erect, and smaller images.
question_patterns: describe a concave lens
what is a diverging lens
nature of image formed by concave lens
how to identify a concave lens by touch
what do you understand by concave lenses

solution_steps.explain: Check if the lens is thinner in the center than at the periphery.
Note that light rays spread out after passing through the lens.
Confirm that the image formed is always virtual, erect, and diminished regardless of object position.

concepts.title: Dispersion of Sunlight
concepts.definition: The process of splitting white light into its seven constituent colors (VIBGYOR).
concepts.key_idea: Sunlight is a mixture of seven colors, visible in rainbows and prisms.
question_patterns: how many colors are in a rainbow
what does a prism do to sunlight
what is Newton's disc
is sunlight white or colored
explain dispersion of sunlight in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Direct a narrow beam of sunlight through a glass prism.
Look for the seven colors appearing on a white screen behind the prism.
Note the sequence of colors from top to bottom: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red (VIBGYOR).

worked_examples.question_pattern: David is observing his image in a plane mirror. The distance between the mirror and his image is {dist_img} m. If he moves {move} m towards the mirror, then what is the distance between David and his image?

extracted_variables.dist_img: initial distance of image from mirror

solution_template.explain: Since initial image distance is dist_img, initial object distance is also dist_img. Moving towards the mirror reduces this.
The distance between object and image is twice the object distance from the mirror.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A driver is reversing his car at a speed of {speed} m/s. At what speed will the image of a stationary truck appear to approach the driver in the plane mirror?

solution_template.explain: In a plane mirror, the image approaches the mirror at the same speed as the object. The relative speed between object and image is double the speed relative to the mirror.
